newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi--Italy pension reform should begin in 97.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi--Italy pension reform should begin in 97.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in remarks published on Thursday that a review of Italy's pension system should not be delayed and he would be satisfied with even a fairly small packet of cost cuts in 1997.
"A radical reform of the reform is not necessary," La Stampa newspaper quoted Ciampi as saying, referring to a landmark 1995 deal to reform Italy's generous pension system.
He said "significant corrective measures" should be set in train swiftly once the initial spending impact of the 1995 deal had been monitored.

"I would be satisfied even with a packet of measures that gave us a saving of, I don't know, one trillion lire in 1997...(That would mean) we would have begun structural intervention on the pension system and would give us prestige and also bring interest rates down more quickly."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi last month urged trades union leaders to discuss a revision of the pension system this year, saying the subject was too important to be delayed.

Unions, backed by the hard-left Communist Refoundation party which is a key government ally, have fiercely opposed moves to bring forward discussions of the 1995 deal which were originally scheduled to begin in 1998.
Economic commentators say the pensions system must be reformed to complete Italy's overhaul of its state finances.
